neg.label: Collective
neg.summary: The state and society steer the economy, share risks and redistribute.

pos.label: Market
pos.summary: Markets, private ownership and low taxes decide most outcomes.

facets.name: Ownership of key sectors
facets.neg: Energy, rail, water, healthcare and housing largely publicly owned.
facets.mid: Mixed: some public services and utilities public, the rest private.
facets.pos: Almost everything private, including healthcare, rail and utilities.

facets.name: Market regulation and housing
facets.neg: Heavy regulation, price and rent controls, large public housing sector.
facets.mid: Targeted rules where markets fail.
facets.pos: Minimal regulation, no price or rent controls.

facets.name: Labour and workers' rights
facets.neg: Strong unions, high minimum wage, strong job protection and co-determination.
facets.mid: Statutory minimum wage and basic protections, otherwise flexible.
facets.pos: Flexible hire and fire, weak or no minimum wage, limited union rights.

facets.name: Tax and welfare
facets.neg: High, steeply progressive taxes funding generous, broad welfare.
facets.mid: Moderately progressive taxes and a conditional safety net.
facets.pos: Low, flat taxes and a minimal safety net.

neg.label: Progressive
neg.summary: Individual choice in private life, active equality policy, secular state.

pos.label: Traditional
pos.summary: Traditional family, religion and moral norms shape law and public life.

facets.name: Family and gender roles
facets.neg: Active gender equality policy, all family forms treated equally.
facets.mid: Formal equality without active steering.
facets.pos: Law and policy promote the traditional family and gender roles.

facets.name: LGBTQ rights
facets.neg: Full equality, legal gender self-identification, strong protections.
facets.mid: Same-sex marriage accepted, cautious on gender identity policy.
facets.pos: Against same-sex marriage, restricts legal gender change.

facets.name: Religion in public life
facets.neg: Strict separation, no public funding or privileges for religion.
facets.mid: Neutral state that accommodates religious institutions.
facets.pos: Religion should guide law, education and public morals.

facets.name: Personal morality laws
facets.neg: Legal abortion on request, euthanasia, regulated drugs and sex work.
facets.mid: Current Western European compromise: some of these legal, under conditions.
facets.pos: Ban or strongly restrict abortion, euthanasia, drugs and sex work.

neg.label: Freedom
neg.summary: Limit state power over citizens, even at some cost to security.

pos.label: Order
pos.summary: Give the state the powers it needs to keep order and security.

facets.name: Surveillance and privacy
facets.neg: No mass surveillance or data retention, strong encryption, no digital ID.
facets.mid: Targeted surveillance with judicial oversight.
facets.pos: Broad surveillance, data retention, camera and ID systems.

facets.name: Policing and justice
facets.neg: Rehabilitation first, shorter sentences, fewer police powers.
facets.mid: Balance between punishment and rehabilitation.
facets.pos: Tough sentencing, more police with broad powers.

facets.name: Limits on speech
facets.neg: Minimal legal limits on speech, protest or content online.
facets.mid: Incitement and direct threats banned, little beyond that.
facets.pos: Broad limits: hate speech and disinformation laws, platform duties, protest or campus restrictions. Counts restrictions from any direction.

facets.name: Emergency and executive powers
facets.neg: Tight limits on emergency powers, lockdowns and restrictions on assembly.
facets.mid: Emergency powers exist with time limits and parliamentary control.
facets.pos: Broad powers to govern by decree and restrict assembly in a crisis.

neg.label: Welcoming
neg.summary: More migration, generous asylum, a civic and plural identity.

pos.label: Restrictive
pos.summary: Much less migration, strict asylum, protect national culture.

facets.name: Immigration levels
facets.neg: Much higher immigration, close to open borders.
facets.mid: Roughly current managed levels.
facets.pos: Near zero or net-negative immigration, including deportations of residents.

facets.name: Asylum and refugees
facets.neg: Generous asylum, more resettlement, fewer detentions.
facets.mid: Refugee Convention obligations met, faster procedures.
facets.pos: Close asylum entirely, leave or ignore the Refugee Convention.

facets.name: Integration
facets.neg: Multicultural model, no assimilation demands.
facets.mid: Language and civic requirements, cultural freedom otherwise.
facets.pos: Strict assimilation, limits on religious or cultural expression.

facets.name: National culture and identity
facets.neg: Civic, post-national identity, de-emphasise national culture.
facets.mid: Pride in national culture without exclusive claims.
facets.pos: Ethno-cultural nationalism, protect the native culture first.

neg.label: Global
neg.summary: Pool sovereignty, trade freely, act through alliances.

pos.label: National
pos.summary: Keep sovereignty, protect the home market, go it alone.

facets.name: Supranational integration
facets.neg: Federal Europe or much stronger international institutions. US frame: UN, WTO, treaties.
facets.mid: Membership with selective cooperation.
facets.pos: Leave the EU or withdraw from international bodies.

facets.name: Trade
facets.neg: Free trade, more trade agreements.
facets.mid: Trade deals with safeguards for some sectors.
facets.pos: Tariffs and protection of domestic industry.

facets.name: Alliances and collective defence
facets.neg: Strong commitment to NATO and allies, firm support for Ukraine.
facets.mid: In alliances, reluctant on commitments abroad.
facets.pos: Leave alliances or non-alignment, no military support abroad. Pacifist and nationalist reasons both count.

facets.name: Development aid
facets.neg: Aid well above 0.7% of GNI.
facets.mid: Around current levels.
facets.pos: Abolish development aid.

neg.label: Ecological
neg.summary: Climate and nature come first, even at real economic cost.

pos.label: Developmental
pos.summary: Growth, affordability and land use come before climate and nature targets.

facets.name: Climate ambition
facets.neg: Net zero well before 2040, legally binding.
facets.mid: Current EU and Paris-aligned targets, flexible on timing.
facets.pos: Abandon targets, climate policy not needed.

facets.name: Transition costs and mandates
facets.neg: Accept high carbon prices and bans on fossil heating and cars.
facets.mid: Carbon pricing with compensation, few bans.
facets.pos: No carbon taxes or mandates, maximise fossil output.

facets.name: Nature and agriculture
facets.neg: Sharp cuts in livestock and nitrogen, large-scale nature restoration.
facets.mid: Gradual measures, farmers compensated.
facets.pos: Farming and development first, scrap nature rules.

facets.name: International climate deals
facets.neg: Strengthen Paris, large climate finance contributions.
facets.mid: Stay in Paris, meet commitments.
facets.pos: Leave Paris and climate finance.

neg.label: Sceptical
neg.summary: Slow down and tightly control new technology.

pos.label: Accelerating
pos.summary: Adopt new technology fast, regulate lightly.

facets.name: AI and automation
facets.neg: Strict limits, moratoria on advanced AI, protect jobs from automation.
facets.mid: Risk-based regulation such as the EU AI Act.
facets.pos: Minimal regulation, push adoption, pre-empt local rules.

facets.name: Biotech and genetics
facets.neg: Ban GMOs and gene editing in food and humans.
facets.mid: Case-by-case approval.
facets.pos: Permissive on GMOs, gene editing and new medical biotech.

facets.name: Nuclear and new energy technology
facets.neg: Phase out nuclear, against CCS and geoengineering.
facets.mid: Keep existing plants, open to research.
facets.pos: Build new nuclear and SMRs, back other new energy technology.

facets.name: Power of big tech
facets.neg: Break up platforms, strong content and data rules.
facets.mid: Competition and data rules like the EU DMA and DSA.
facets.pos: Leave platforms largely alone.

neg.label: Institutional
neg.summary: Trust and defend institutions, experts, courts and representative democracy.

pos.label: Vox populi
pos.summary: The people against the elite, direct democracy, curb unelected power.

facets.name: Trust in institutions and experts
facets.neg: Defends institutions, experts and established media.
facets.mid: Critical but loyal to the system.
facets.pos: Institutions, experts and media seen as a hostile elite.

facets.name: Direct democracy
facets.neg: Purely representative, no referendums.
facets.mid: Occasional consultative referendums.
facets.pos: Binding referendums and citizens' initiatives on most issues.

facets.name: Power of the courts
facets.neg: Strong independent courts with constitutional review.
facets.mid: Independent courts, parliament has the last word.
facets.pos: Curb judges and judicial review, more political control.

facets.name: Centralisation
facets.neg: Strong regional or local autonomy, up to independence.
facets.mid: Current division of power.
facets.pos: Power concentrated at national level.
